marks.gloss_en: דרבה בר בר חנה קאי כוותיה -- R' Yochanan (via Rabba bar bar Chana) reads the baraita's prohibition of the slaughtered hanging limb as only a mitzva of separation, so slaughter does not make it fallen

the baraita: 'and flesh torn in the field you shall not eat' (Ex 22:30) -- to include the limb and the flesh hanging on a domestic animal, a wild animal or a bird, that one slaughtered: they are forbidden
בשלמא לרבי שמעון בן לקיש -- לדבריהם קאמר להו: לדידי לא שנא אבר דעובר ולא שנא אבר דבהמה, כי הדדי נינהו -- he argued on the Sages' terms
והא הוכשרו קתני! -- the mishna says 'they' were made susceptible, plural, so not the flesh alone
מהו דתימא: חד לבשר הפורש מן הבהמה, וחד לבשר הפורש מן האבר (= p_trei_basar)
you might say: [the plural is] one for flesh separating from the animal and one for flesh separating from the limb
ומאי אולמיה דהאי מהאי? -- why would the one kind of flesh need stating more than the other?
סלקא דעתך אמינא: הואיל ומטמא טומאה חמורה אגב אביו, אימא לא ליבעי הכשר -- קמשמע לן
the dictum is about the limb of a fetus
R' Yochanan (version 2): but in an animal's [hanging] limb all agree that slaughter does not make [it] fallen
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: R' Yochanan's reason for R' Meir -- this [hanging limb] is her body, and that [fetus's limb] is not her body
R' Yochanan: all agree that death makes [a hanging limb] fallen
the mishna: if the animal died -- the [hanging] flesh needs hechsher, and the limb imparts impurity as a limb from the living, not as a limb from a carcass; the words of R' Meir
the mishna: if the animal was slaughtered -- they were made susceptible by its blood; the words of R' Meir
from that [mishna] I would have said: 'they were made susceptible' refers to the flesh [only]
